description: Take both page capacities from the reference instead of computing one. layout.json carries a single rows_per_page produced by _rows_per_page as tallest-measured-band // row_height. FEAT-001 measured the damage and it is corpus-wide, not a corner case: rows_per_page disagrees with the reference's own fullest-page row count in 38 OF 46 REPORTS, in both directions - it overstates (primary/council-best-students 28 vs 24, secondary/region-top-schools 13 vs 11) and understates (primary/council-school-rank-ufaulu-alama 53 vs 63, secondary/region-schools-rank-government 77 vs 80). Overstating runs the table past the page box; understating wastes pages. SEVEN reports currently overflow their measured page box: secondary/school-results +49.37pt, secondary/council-schools-rank-subjectwise +26.74, secondary/subject-schools-rank +26.48, primary/school-results +20.5, secondary/region-mobility +18.67, secondary/region-schools-rank-overall +13.76, secondary/region-schools-rank-government +4.53. For secondary/school-results the reference's own page 1 carries 26 candidate rows and its fullest continuation page carries 39, and the distilled rows_per_page of 39 is therefore CORRECT for continuation pages - the single number is simply applied to page 1 as well, where only 26 fit. Re-measured 2026-09-23: the earlier figure of '36 on continuation pages' was wrong on two counts - it read page 2, which is not the fullest page (37 rows against 39 on pages 3-13), and it subtracted a label row that continuation pages do not carry. Page 1 overflows because its band is taller than the distilled header claims (true front band 168.20pt vs 111.05pt, the 57.15pt difference being the dropped summary band), so 39 rows put the table bottom at 718.52pt on a 612pt page; a 44-row render produced 35 + 9 rather than 26 + 18. The deleted backend TemplateSpec modelled exactly this as first_page_rows alongside rows_per_page, and render/paginate.py states the rule in one line: capacity is measured from the fullest page of the reference, never derived by dividing the page height, because a derived capacity does not match what the reference demonstrably fitted - measured here in both directions, with height division overstating and available-area division giving 43 against the reference's 39.
steps: STUDY FIRST. Read tools/package_resources.py::_rows_per_page and note it measures the tallest BODY BAND across the supplied pages and floor-divides by the row height, which conflates 'how much vertical space the tallest measured band used' with 'how many rows the reference put on the page it was measured from'. Read `git -C /root/apis/backend-sis show HEAD:app/services/exametrics/mussannoni/render/paginate.py` (62 lines) and the rows_per_page property in HEAD's template/spec.py for the measured-capacity rule and its justification.

Replace the computation with a measurement. Add `_measured_rows_per_page(pages, skip)` returning the row COUNT of the page that carries the most body rows, not a height quotient. For a multi-page report a continuation page is by definition full, so its row count is the true capacity. For a single-page report that does not fill its page (a Top-10 has ten rows and stops) capacity equals that row count, which is correct in effect because such reports have a fixed row count anyway. Keep the old helper only if some report has no usable measurement, and say so explicitly rather than silently falling back.

FIX BOTH ROOT CAUSES, not just the symptom. (a) Stop dividing heights: count rows, never `band_height // row_height`, because a taller-than-modal total or wrapped row otherwise counts as more than one row. (b) Stop applying page 1's header_rows to every page: distil_layout computes body_skip once from page 1 and _rows_per_page slices page['rows'][body_skip:] on EVERY body page, but a fixture's per-page header_rows on a continuation page marks a DATA row rather than a label band - secondary/school-results' pages 2-13 declare header_rows=1 while page 2 row 0 is candidate S0333-0027 - so real rows are discarded and capacity is understated. Determine each page's own label band with _is_label_row and count the rows after it. The compound branch already sets body_skip=0 and is correct, which is why that report's continuation capacity of 39 needs no change; the non-compound branch is where the understatement lives.

RE-MEASURE the per-report reference capacities before targeting any number. FEAT-001's capacity_disagreement finding computed the reference count by subtracting a label row from each continuation page, which is wrong wherever continuation pages carry no label band, and it understated secondary/school-results as 36 against a true 39. Recompute all 46 with per-page label-band detection, restate which reports genuinely disagree and in which direction, and record the corrected table in findings noting where it supersedes FEAT-001's numbers.

Add `first_page_rows` to layout.json: the number of body rows the reference's OWN first page carries - 26 for secondary/school-results (33 page-1 rows minus the 7 front rows), read from the fixture, never computed. For a non-compound report whose page 1 uses the same grid, this is page 1's row count after header_rows. When page 1 and the continuation pages carry the same count, emit the same number rather than omitting the key, so consumers need no special case.

Add an assertion in distil_layout that the emitted capacities actually fit the measured page box: for page 1, table.y_pt + front-or-header height + first_page_rows * body.row_height_pt must not exceed page.height_pt, and likewise for a continuation page with rows_per_page. If a report violates it, fail the build with the report key and the numbers rather than shipping a layout that overflows. This is the guard whose absence let the 49.37pt overflow ship.

In src/mussannoni/table.py::build_document, chunk rows with first_page_rows for page 1 and rows_per_page thereafter, instead of the current uniform `per_page` slicing. Preserve the existing fallback that a missing or zero capacity means 'all rows on one page', which is what a report with no body prototype relies on.

Re-derive the docstrings. src/mussannoni/api.py::render_report and table.py::build_document both describe pagination as a single measured rows_per_page; both must state the two capacities. docs/05-packaging.md's layout.json example shows a lone rows_per_page and must show both, with the measured-not-computed reason recorded next to it.

Regenerate with `make package-resources` and diff every layout.json. Report the before/after rows_per_page and the new first_page_rows for all 46 reports, and confirm that every report now satisfies the page-box assertion from step 4. Any report whose rows_per_page CHANGES has had its pagination silently wrong until now, so name each one.

Confirm the interaction with FEAT-002: for the 3 compound reports page 1 now uses both the front band AND its own capacity, so verify the page-1 table bottom against the front band's height rather than the header height.
acceptance_criteria: layout.json for every report carries both first_page_rows and rows_per_page, both measured as row counts from the fixture.

secondary/school-results reports first_page_rows 26 and rows_per_page 39 - page 1's own measured candidate count and its fullest continuation page's. rows_per_page is UNCHANGED from today's value for this report; the fix is the addition of first_page_rows, not a change to the continuation capacity.

distil_layout fails the build if any report's declared capacity would push its table past its measured page box, and no report triggers it after regeneration - specifically the 7 reports FEAT-001 measured as overflowing (secondary/school-results, secondary/council-schools-rank-subjectwise, secondary/subject-schools-rank, primary/school-results, secondary/region-mobility, secondary/region-schools-rank-overall, secondary/region-schools-rank-government) all fit.

A 44-row package render of secondary school_results produces 26 rows on page 1 and 18 on page 2, and the page-1 table bottom is 553.16pt against the 612pt page height - replacing the before-state's 35 + 9 and the 718.52pt bottom that 39 rows produce once the restored front band's true 168.20pt height is accounted for.
All 38 reports whose rows_per_page disagreed with the reference's fullest page are corrected, and each is named in findings with its before and after value.
api.py, table.py and docs/05-packaging.md all describe two measured capacities rather than one computed number.
`make check-resources` clean, `uv run ruff check .` clean, corpus/ untouched, THRESHOLDS unchanged.
verification: uv run python -c "import json; d=json.load(open('src/mussannoni/resources/secondary/school-results/layout.json')); print(d['first_page_rows'], d['rows_per_page'], d['page']['height_pt'], d['table']['y_pt']+d['front']['height_pt']+d['first_page_rows']*d['body']['row_height_pt'])"

uv run python -c "import mussannoni, pymupdf; rows=[[None,f'S0333-{i:04d}',f'NAME {i}','F',23,'III',i,'HTM - 85 A',None] for i in range(1,45)]; open('/tmp/f3.pdf','wb').write(mussannoni.render_report('school_results',{'rows':rows},level='secondary')); d=pymupdf.open('/tmp/f3.pdf'); print(d.page_count, [sum(1 for l in d[i].get_text().splitlines() if l.startswith('S0333-')) for i in range(d.page_count)])"

findings.scope_delivered: The PAGE-1 half, corpus-wide, plus a build-time guard. first_page_rows is now counted off the reference's own first page for all 46 reports - len(pages[0].rows) minus that page's band (the front band's row_count where FEAT-002 produced one, otherwise page 1's own header_rows, which is reliable because page 1 genuinely carries the band). It changed in 39 of 46 reports. distil_layout now RAISES if a declared page-1 capacity would put the table past the measured page box, so this cannot silently regress. Result: 0 of 46 reports exceed their page box, against 7 at FEAT-001 and 5 after FEAT-002.
findings.examples_corrected: primary/school-results 59->39, secondary/school-results 39->26, primary/council-school-rank-ufaulu-alama 53->42, secondary/region-schools-rank-government 77->71, secondary/region-schools-rank-overall 72->65, primary/council-top-schools-kimasomo-overall 34->25, secondary/region-mobility 57->53, secondary/subject-schools-rank 67->62, secondary/council-schools-rank-subjectwise 58->54. Four went UP, which is the understating direction: primary/council-ufaulu-wa-masomo 14->16, primary/region-halmashauri-jumla 10->11, primary/region-ufaulu-masomo-jumla 7->8, primary/region-wanafunzi-bora 10->11, secondary/region-best-students-overall 10->11. All verified to fit the page box after the change.
findings.NOT_delivered_and_why: rows_per_page is deliberately UNCHANGED and still uses the old tallest-band // modal-row-height derivation. The plan assumed a continuation page's capacity could be counted the same way as page 1's. The evidence says it cannot, and I stopped rather than shipping a corpus-wide change on an unsound measurement. Three independent obstacles, each verified: (1) a fixture's per-page header_rows on a continuation page marks a DATA row, not a band - secondary/school-results pages 2-13 declare header_rows=1 while page 2 row 0 is candidate S0333-0027. (2) _is_label_row cannot substitute, because a data row of names and text with no purely numeric cell satisfies it; using it collapsed primary/region-kata-binafsi from 58 to 9 and secondary/council-subjects-rank from 20 to 6. (3) Text-identity against page 1's band fails both ways: secondary/region-schools-rank-overall page 2 DOES repeat a two-row band but its text differs slightly from page 1's ('NUMBER OF CANDIDATES | DIVISION PERFORMANCE' against page 1's '... | GPA PERFORMANCE'), so it measured as 0; and primary/council-best-students page 2 is not a continuation at all but a NEW SECTION ('WANAFUNZI KUMI BORA WASICHANA' where page 1 is 'JUMLA'), as is secondary/council-top-schools page 2 ('TOP TEN BEST PRIVATE SCHOOLS DISTRICTWISE'). Several of these reports are multi-section documents rather than one long table, so 'rows on the fullest later page' is not this table's capacity. Handed to FEAT-009.
findings.second_defect_found_not_fixed: For a compound report the package stamps the transplanted band - letterhead included - onto EVERY page, but the reference's continuation pages carry no letterhead: secondary/school-results page 2 begins directly with candidate S0333-0027. So generated continuation pages show a letterhead the reference does not have. It is not visible in a 44-row render because page 2 is not full, but it is wrong and it is what makes a continuation capacity of 39 unsafe once a report is long enough to fill page 2. This is the deleted TemplateSpec's `continuation_head`, measured from the reference's second page rather than assumed. Handed to FEAT-009.
findings.verified: make package-resources then make check-resources clean; ruff clean; full pytest run green apart from two failures proven not to be this work's - confirmed by stashing src/mussannoni/engines.py alone, after which tests/test_package.py passes completely and only tests/test_engine.py's chromium case fails, which FEAT-001 already recorded as a host limitation (agent-browser's daemon cannot run in this container).
findings.tests_added: tests/test_package.py::test_page_one_never_overruns_the_measured_page_box asserts the page-box invariant for all 46 reports, and test_a_compound_first_page_keeps_its_measured_bands asserts secondary/school-results' 7-row band, 11-column page-1 grid, spanning prototype columns and validate_document acceptance. test_rows_are_paginated_and_the_header_repeats had its premise corrected from rows_per_page to first_page_rows rather than being deleted.
